question: Plot a Gantt-style timeline for patients, showing the duration of treatments, hospitalizations, and follow-up visits. Use color to distinguish event types and include patient IDs on the y-axis.

files.eval_guideline: Gantt chart must show horizontal event bars for each patient with distinct colors per event type (treatment, hospitalization, follow-up) and a legend; patient ordering, color scheme, and styling may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files have the identical basename gantt_patient_events.png and PNG image format. The filename directly corresponds to the requested Gantt-style patient event timeline for task b-3-14.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires visual content: horizontal event bars for each patient, distinct colors for treatment, hospitalization, and follow-up, and a legend. Semantic comparison can assess these requirements and patient ID labels while allowing differences in patient ordering, colors, and styling.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images show Gantt-style timelines for the same ten patients, Patient_01 through Patient_10, across January–July 2023. They display matching treatment and hospitalization intervals and follow-up visit patterns using horizontal bars, distinct event colors, and appropriate legends. The patient order, date scale, and overall clinical event sequences agree. The candidate separates event types vertically within each patient's row, making overlapping treatments and hospitalizations easier to distinguish, whereas the reference overlays them on a shared baseline. The candidate also places its legend outside the plotting area, revealing late follow-up visits obscured by the reference legend. Differences in color shades, bar thickness, grid styling, title, and date-label formatting are cosmetic. No meaningful data discrepancy or missing scientific element is apparent.
